prompt:
Optimize the inventory history API `stock.history.balances(events, checkpoints)` so a large reconciliation batch does not rescan all movements per checkpoint. Keep the `Movement(event_id, revision, sku, at, delta)` and `Checkpoint(sku, at)` dataclasses and the public API unchanged.

Both arguments are finite iterables, possibly one-shot generators. Movement IDs/SKUs are strings; revision, at and delta are integers (timestamps may be integer subclasses with instrumented comparisons). A movement ID may have several revisions: use the highest revision; when revisions tie, the last occurrence in the input wins. IDs are global, so a revision can move an event to a different SKU or timestamp. Only the winning revision contributes. Every winning movement adds its signed delta to its SKU at its timestamp. Each checkpoint returns the sum of that SKU's deltas at times <= checkpoint.at, starting from zero. Preserve checkpoint input order, duplicates, and negative balances; unknown SKUs return zero. Events/checkpoints may be unsorted or empty. Do not modify records or caller-owned lists. Return a list of integers.

Required complexity: O((E+Q) log(E+Q)) time or better and O(E+Q) space, where E is all input events including superseded revisions and Q is checkpoints. Hidden performance checks count timestamp comparisons, not wall-clock time: on 5,000 unique movements and 5,000 checkpoints for one SKU, use at most 24*(E+Q)*ceil(log2(E+Q+2)) timestamp comparisons. Do not convert/coerce timestamps to bypass their comparisons. Preserve integer timestamp semantics; sorting and binary search or an ordered sweep are appropriate. Keep small-input behavior and add regression tests for revisions and boundaries.
